messages:
maria: Heads-up — we started seeing backpressure on console queries for some large accounts. p95 token/time spikes, and a handful of 503s. Anyone tracking this?
kevin: Yup, noticed it around 09:12 UTC. Happens when dashboards with many panels (>=8) load simultaneously. Query layer queues back up.
jamie: Is this the regular /console/query path or something new?
maria: Same /console/query endpoint. Frontend fan-out is the culprit — each panel fires independent queries (embeddings, long-range aggregates).
sasha: Short-term fixes: add per-connection concurrency limits and 429s. Long-term: consider server-side merge of panel queries into a single composite request.
kevin: Merging sounds ideal for throughput but raises RBAC complexity — each subquery might have different row-level filters. Merged execution needs to preserve scopes.
maria: Exactly. We can't just run with elevated perms. We either run per-subquery filters in the merged plan or execute per-scope in sequence (slower).
jamie: Another approach: async execution with a bounded worker pool + status_url (202 + polling or websocket push). Pros: bounded load, natural backpressure. Cons: higher latency for cold dashboards and more frontend code.
sasha: Also caching: per-panel TTLs and stale-while-revalidate could cut load heavily for idle dashboards. Need eviction keyed by team+panel.
kevin: For async, we need to decide where RBAC is enforced: at enqueue, at execute, or both. Enforce at enqueue to avoid waste, but re-check at exec to handle policy changes.
maria: Good point — we should fail explicitly if scope has narrowed between enqueue and run. UX: panel shows permission error, not stale data.
jamie: I'm going to draft a brief RFC comparing three options: (1) proxy+merge, (2) async queue with status_url, (3) strict rate-limit + graceful degradation (partial panels). Will include RBAC and perf tradeoffs.
sasha: Add cost metrics to the RFC: per-panel token cost, average tokens per dashboard load, queue depth histograms. That'll help prioritize.
maria: Can eng-platform add traces that include panel_id, auth_scope, and tokens_consumed? That would make debugging easier.
kevin: I can add a small trace patch — will emit panel_id and scope as tags (no payload data).
jamie: To avoid breaking API, propose Accept: prefer-async header as opt-in for frontend. Server returns 202 + status_url when queued, otherwise 200 for sync.
maria: Frontend team ok to wire that in — they can toggle per-experiment.
sasha: Edge cases: RBAC changes, partial-results when a subset of subqueries succeed, and cache invalidation when different teams share a panel. We'll list these as must-handle in RFC.
jamie: Drafting now. Perf targets suggestion: cached p95 <600ms, async best-effort <2s to first-status, queue backlog <30s under target load.
maria: Thanks — please comment by EOD Thursday and I'll collate.
deploy-bot: Heads-up: we have the prod rollout window next Tue 02:00 UTC if we want a staged canary. :rocket:
